The '''1970–71 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|68th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|39th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

==Summary==
The club finished in a disappointing fourth place, two points below Champion [[Valencia CF]] coached by former Real Madrid' star [[Alfredo Di Stéfano]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=as.com|title=The Dilemma of Real Madrid in 1971|url=http://www.as.com/static/pdf/ascolor/03/numero3_ok.pdf|access-date=7 June 2020}}</ref>

In [[1971 Copa del Generalísimo]] the squad as Defending Champion was early eliminated in Round of 32 by [[Deportivo La Coruña]] on away goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/copa71.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030917233809/http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa71.htm|url-status=usurped|archive-date=17 September 2003|publisher=linguasport.com|title= Copa del Generalísimo 1971}}</ref>

It was the club's first absence in the European Cup. The team played the 7th final in Europe, a record at the time,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2018/12/14/the-emperors-of-athens-how-chelsea-won-the-cup-winners-cup-in-1971/|publisher=thesefootballtimes.co|title=The Emperors of Athens}}</ref> first a draw 1–1 after extra time,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/incoming/article5638.ece/BINARY/Chelsea+2-1+Real+Madrid|work=Daily Mirror|title=Ole, Ole Chelsea|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> and then, lost the [[1971 European Cup Winners' Cup Final]] trophy against [[Chelsea F.C.]] 1–2 in the replay in [[Piraeus]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/incoming/article155173.ece/BINARY/Chelsea+1-1+Real+Madrid|publisher=mirrorfootball.co.uk|title=Real Shock for Chelsea|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> closing the first trophy-less season since the 1952–53 campaign. After 18 years as club player, clinching 12 league titles, 2 Copa del Generalísimo and 6 European Cups [[Francisco Gento]] is retired at the end of this season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1996/02/01/deportes/823129214_850215.html|title=Gento|work=El País|access-date=1 July 2020|language=Spanish}}</ref>
